translationRepairs: Prince Xi Jinjian of Ji, also Shizong's son, was enfeoffed in Xiande 6 and died in the second year of the Song Qiande era.
Prince Xi Jin of Ji, also Shizong's son, was enfeoffed in Xiande 6 and died in the second year of the Song Qiande era.

Focus unit names 紀王熙謹; 謹 is the single syllable jǐn, so Xi Jinjian is a false three-syllable reading. Sibling forms 熙讓/熙誨 as Xi Rang/Xi Hui confirm the two-character Xi X pattern. The proposed Xi Jin is accurate.
Prince of Ji Xi Jinjian, a son of Shizong, was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Xiande and died in the second year of Qiande of the present dynasty.
Prince of Ji Xi Jin, a son of Shizong, was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Xiande and died in the second year of Qiande of the present dynasty.
Same focus unit 紀王熙謹; the literal's Xi Jinjian mis-romanizes 謹. Replacing with Xi Jin restores the correct two-syllable given name without other changes.

Ouyang Xiu's family biographies record seven sons of Shizong: the eldest Yige, two younger boys still unnamed, then the future Emperor Gong, then Xi Rang, Xi Jinjian, and Xi Hui. Their mothers are unknown. Yige and the two unnamed boys were killed by the Later Han.

Ouyang Xiu's family biographies record seven sons of Shizong: the eldest Yige, two younger boys still unnamed, then the future Emperor Gong, then Xi Rang, Xi Jin, and Xi Hui. Their mothers are unknown. Yige and the two unnamed boys were killed by the Later Han.

The unit's 熙謹 must be Xi Jin, not Xi Jinjian. Inserting parenthetical 宜哥 after Yige is unnecessary here: Yige already romanizes 宜哥, and the gloss is stylistic disambiguation against a different chapter's 意哥 rather than a repair of this wording.

The "Biographies of the Imperial Family" in Ouyang's History says: Shizong had seven sons; the eldest was called Yige, the next two were both unnamed, the next was the Emperor Gong, then Xi Rang, Xi Jinjian, and Xi Hui; it is not known who their mothers were; Yige and the other two were all executed by the Han.

The "Biographies of the Imperial Family" in Ouyang's History says: Shizong had seven sons; the eldest was called Yige, the next two were both unnamed, the next was the Emperor Gong, then Xi Rang, Xi Jin, and Xi Hui; it is not known who their mothers were; Yige and the other two were all executed by the Han.
Literal likewise needs Xi Jin for 熙謹. The added (宜哥) glosses are not required by this Chinese; keep Yige alone and correct only the romanization error.
Xi Jinjian and Xi Hui had never held titles; now Xi Jinjian was made Grand General of the Right Martial Guard and Prince of Ji;
Xi Jin and Xi Hui had never held titles; now Xi Jin was made Grand General of the Right Martial Guard and Prince of Ji;
Unit 熙謹、熙誨……拜熙謹 names the same prince twice; both English Xi Jinjian readings are wrong. Xi Jin matches 謹 and parallels Xi Hui for 熙誨.
Xi Jinjian and Xi Hui had both previously received no noble rank; thereupon Xi Jinjian was appointed Grand General of the Right Martial Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Ji;
Xi Jin and Xi Hui had both previously received no noble rank; thereupon Xi Jin was appointed Grand General of the Right Martial Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Ji;
Literal repeats the same double misreading of 熙謹 as Xi Jinjian; both occurrences correctly become Xi Jin.
Xi Jinjian died in the tenth month of Qiande 2; what became of Xi Rang and Xi Hui is not recorded. (End of editorial note.)〉
Xi Jin died in the tenth month of Qiande 2; what became of Xi Rang and Xi Hui is not recorded. (End of editorial note.)〉
Unit 熙謹卒 records this prince's death; idiomatic Xi Jinjian is the same romanization error. Xi Jin is correct; the rest of the sentence is fine.
In the tenth month of the second year of Qiande, Xi Jinjian died; the final fates of Xi Rang and Xi Hui are unknown. (End of editorial note.)〉
In the tenth month of the second year of Qiande, Xi Jin died; the final fates of Xi Rang and Xi Hui are unknown. (End of editorial note.)〉
Literal's Xi Jinjian for 熙謹 is likewise wrong; Xi Jin restores the name without altering the Qiande 2 death notice or the unknown fates of 熙讓 and 熙誨.
